subject: chemistry
title: Equilibrium Adventure 1: Dynamic equilibrium and Kc
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet dynamic equilibrium and the equilibrium constant Kc.
meta_desc: IBDP Chemistry — dynamic equilibrium, Kc expression, position vs constant.
final_note: You learned equilibrium is dynamic (forward = reverse rate), Kc = [products]^x / [reactants]^y, large Kc favours products.

walkthroughs.body_html:
For aA + bB ⇌ cC + dD: in a closed system, forward rate eventually equals reverse rate.

Concentrations are constant, but molecules still react both ways.

Macroscopic stasis, microscopic action.

Kc = [C]^c [D]^d / [A]^a [B]^b

Only at equilibrium. Pure solids and liquids excluded.

Large Kc (>> 1): equilibrium lies to the right (mostly products).
Small Kc (<< 1): lies to the left (mostly reactants).
Kc ≈ 1: comparable amounts.

N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, Kc = [NH₃]² / ([N₂][H₂]³).

For H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g): at 500 K, Kc ≈ 60.

If at equilibrium [H₂] = 0.10, [I₂] = 0.10, then [HI]² = Kc × [H₂][I₂] = 60 × 0.01 = 0.60, so [HI] = 0.77 mol dm⁻³.
